bear.last: RENDER/USD: Shorting RENDER/USD after an already brutal -21.58% 20-day collapse is textbook chasing into an oversold hole with an RSI14 of 37.09 and a z-score of -1.26. Worse, the pair trades in a complete liquidity desert with a 20-day average dollar volume of just $3,325 and a volume ratio of 0.0, directly violating our desk lesson to skip trades where liquidity cannot sustain execution or risk-to-reward. In a market this thin, entering a short invites catastrophic slippage, unmanageable borrow risk, and explosive squeeze vulnerability on negligible buy volume. Historical ATR behavior shows sharp upside asymmetry: within 5 days, upward moves hit 1.0 ATR 57 times versus only 30 times downward, and hit 2.0 ATR 28 times versus just 3 times down. With price sitting close to its 20-day low of $1.44941 and targeting $1.4334 against an ATR of $0.1356 (8.62%), the meager 9% downside potential nowhere near justifies the extreme tail risk of a low-volume blowout.
